correctness.rationale: The quotient on 31^2=961 nonempty ordered color supports is exactly induced by the original synchronous rule, since only opposite-shore blinking membership enters the local update. Support sizes cannot increase. Each periodic support cycle must therefore induce color permutations, whose orders give genuine least microscopic periods; the first periodic time of the full state equals that of its support. An exhaustive independent 961-state transition enumeration finds 16 recurrent support cycles, 49 periodic support states, and maximum depth 25 with witness (1,31). A second exact enumeration computes the 5/6/18 support monodromy classes and supports the surjection-weighted formulas; a complete 961-row support certificate is embedded. The code also checks 64 parameter pairs and microscopically enumerates 97,525 labelled states, including K3,4, checking first entry and least period. The proof for all a,b depends on the finite exact support factor and permutation lifting, not inference from bounded trials.

value.rationale: Complete orbit and global basin invariants are natural for phase-coupled oscillator models. The theorem finds an all-size 25-step cutoff, a complete 5/6/18 period census, exact basin coefficients, and no transient predecessors to period-18 cycles. Most strikingly, N18(n,n) grows as 12^n/3 and dominates the number of periodic orbits, whereas almost every uniformly selected initial state enters a period-5 orbit at exactly 8 steps. The difference between uniform-orbit and uniform-initial-condition statistics is mathematically significant and is not explained by prior qualitative star/tree synchronization criteria. Full classification, not an arbitrary small-parameter observation, motivates the finite count.
